text:
A block of mass m attached to a massless spring is performing oscillatory motion of amplitude ‘A’ on
a frictionless horizontal plane. If half of the mass of the block breaks off when it is passing through
its equilibrium point, the amplitude of oscillation for the remaining system become fA. The value of
f is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At equilibrium position

$V_{0} = V$

$V_{0}=ω_{1}A=\sqrt{\frac{K}{m}}A$ .....(i)

$V=ωA^{1}=\sqrt{\frac{K}{\frac{m}{2}}}A^{1}$ .....(ii)

$\therefore$ $A^{1}=\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
The mass density of a planet of radius R varies with the distance r from its centre as

$ρ$(r) = $ρ_{0}\left (1-\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right )$.

Then the gravitational field is maximum at :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


dm = $ρ$dv

$\int dm$ $=\int ρ_{0}4πr^{2}dr$

$\Rightarrow$ M = $\int ρ_{0}4πr^{2}dr$

Also E = $\frac{GM}{r^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow Er^{2}=4πG\int\limits _{0}^{r}ρ_{0}\left (1-\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right )r^{2}dr$

$\Rightarrow E=4πGρ_{0}\left (\frac{r}{3}-\frac{r^{3}}{5R^{2}}\right )$

For maximum E, $\frac{dE}{dr}=0$

$\frac{1}{3}-\frac{3r^{2}}{5R^{2}}$ = 0

$\therefore$ $r=\sqrt{\frac{5}{9}}R$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Two sources of light emit X-rays of wavelength 1 nm and visible light of wavelength 500 nm, respectively. Both the sources emit light of the same power 200 W. The ratio of the number density of
photons of X-rays to the number density of photons of the visible light of the given wavelengths is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, wavelength of x ray ($λ_{1}$) = 1 nm

And wavelength of visible light ($λ_{2}$) = 500 nm

we know, Power$(P)=\frac{nhc}{λ}$

As P = constant and h, c also constant

So, $\frac{n}{λ}=constant$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{n_{1}}{n_{2}}=\frac{λ_{1}}{λ_{2}}=\frac{1nm}{500nm}=\frac{1}{500}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
A particle is moving unidirectionally on a horizontal plane under the action of a constant power
supplying energy source. The displacement (s) - time (t) graph that describes the motion of the
particle is (graphs are drawn schematically and are not to scale) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P=Fv$

$P=m\frac{dv}{dt}v$

$\Rightarrow$ $vdv=\frac{P}{m}dt$

Integrating both sides, we get

$V^{2}=k^{'}t$

$\Rightarrow$ V = k"$\sqrt{t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{ds}{dt}$ = k"$\sqrt{t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\int ds=\int k^{''}\sqrt{t}dt$

$\Rightarrow$ s $\propto$ $t^{3/2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Which of the following will NOT be observed when a multimeter (operating in resistance measuring
mode) probes connected across a component, are just reversed?
options:
Multimeter shows NO deflection in both cases i.e. before and after reversing the probes if the
chosen component is metal wire.
Multimeter shows a deflection, accompanied by a splash of light out of connected component in one direction and NO deflection on reversing the probes if the chosen component is LED.

Multimeter shows an equal deflection in both cases i.e. before and after reversing the probes if
the chosen component is resistor.

Multimeter shows NO deflection in both cases i.e. before and after reversing the probes if the
chosen component is capacitor.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(1) Multimeter shows deflection when it connects with capacitor.

(2) If we assume that LED has negligible resistance then multimeter shows no deflection for the forward bias but when it connects in reverse direction, it break down occurs so splash of light out.

(3) The resistance of metal wire may be taken zero, so no deflection in multimeter.

(4) No matter, how we connect the resistance across multimeter. It shows same deflection.

text:
A uniform rod of length ‘$l$’ is pivoted at one of its ends on a vertical shaft of negligible radius.
When the shaft rotates at angular speed $ω$ the rod makes an angle $θ$ with it (see figure). To find $θ$
equate the rate of change of angular momentum (direction going into the paper) $\frac{ml^{2}}{12}ω^{2}\sin θ\cos θ$
about the centre of mass (CM) to the torque provided by the horizontal and vertical forces $F_{H}$
 and
$F_{V}$
 about the CM. The value of $θ$ is then such that :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$F_{v}=mg$

$F_{H}=mω^{2}\frac{l}{2}\sin θ$

$\therefore$ $τ_{net}aboutCOM=F_{v}.\frac{l}{2}\sin θ-F_{H}\frac{l}{2}\cos θ$

$=\frac{ml^{2}}{12}ω^{2}\sin θ\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $mg\frac{l}{2}\sin θ-mω^{2}\frac{l}{2}\sin θ\frac{l}{2}\cos θ=\frac{ml^{2}}{12}ω^{2}\sin θ\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow \frac{gl}{2}-\frac{ω^{2}l^{2}}{4}\cos θ=\frac{l^{2}}{12}ω^{2}\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{gl}{2}=ω^{2}l^{2}\cos θ\left (\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{4}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{gl}{2}=\frac{ω^{2}l^{2}\cos θ}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\cos θ=\frac{3g}{2ω^{2}l}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
A block of mass 1.9 kg is at rest at the edge of a table, of height 1 m. A bullet of mass 0.1 kg
collides with the block and sticks to it. If the velocity of the bullet is 20 m/s in the horizontal
direction just before the collision then the kinetic energy just before the combined system strikes
the floor, is [Take $g = 10 m/s^{2}$
 . Assume there is no rotational motion and loss of energy after the
collision is negligible.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let velocity of block after collision = v

Using momentum conservation,

$p_{i} = p_{f}$

0.1×20 = (1.9 + 0.1)V

$\Rightarrow$ 2 = 2 V

$\Rightarrow$ V = 1 m/sec

Kinetic energy just before striking the floor

= $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}+mgh$

= $\frac{1}{2}\times 2(1)^{2}+2\times 10\times 1$

= 21 J

text:
To raise the temperature of a certain mass of gas by $50^{o}C$ at a constant pressure, 160 calories of
heat is required. When the same mass of gas is cooled by $100^{o}C$ at constant volume, 240 calories
of heat is released. How many degrees of freedom does each molecule of this gas have (assume
gas to be ideal)?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$160=nC_{p}50$ ....(i)

$240=nC_{v}100$ ....(ii)

Dividing (i) by (ii), we get

$\frac{160}{240}=\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}\times \frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}$ = $\frac{4}{3}$

We know,

$γ=\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}=1+\frac{2}{f}=\frac{4}{3}$

$\Rightarrow f=6$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
A uniform magnetic field B exists in a direction perpendicular to the plane of a square loop made of
a metal wire. The wire has a diameter of 4 mm and a total length of 30 cm. The magnetic field
changes with time at a steady rate $\frac{dB}{dt}$ $= 0.032 Ts^{–1}$. The induced current in the loop is close to
(Resistivity of the metal wire is 1.23 $\times$ $10^{–8}$ $\Omega$m)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $𝜙=BA$

Also, $E=\frac{d𝜙}{dt}=\frac{AdB}{dt}$

$E=l^{2}\frac{dB}{dt}$

$i=\frac{E}{R}$

= $\frac{l^{2}\frac{dB}{dt}}{\frac{ρl}{A}}$

$=\frac{l^{2}}{pl}\frac{dB}{dt}A$

= $\frac{l^{2}πR^{2}}{ρl}\frac{dB}{dt}$

$\therefore$ $i=\frac{30}{4}\times \frac{30}{4}\times \frac{10^{-4}\times 0.032\times 4\times 10^{-6}\times π}{1.23\times 10^{-8}\times 30\times 10^{-2}\times 10^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $i=\frac{240\times π\times 10^{-10}}{1.23\times 10^{-7}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $i=\frac{240\times 3.14\times 10^{-3}}{1.23}$

$=\frac{753.6}{1.23}\times 10^{-3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $i=612.68\times 10^{-3}=0.61A$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
A block starts moving up an inclined plane of inclination $30^{o}$ with an initial velocity of $v_{0}$
. It comes
back to its initial position with velocity $\frac{v_{0}}{2}$. The value of the coefficient of kinetic friction between
the block and the inclined plane is close to $\frac{I}{1000}$. The nearest integer to $I is____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a block of mass $m$ on the incline ($θ=30^{\circ }$), kinetic friction $μmg\cos θ$ opposes the motion both while it goes up and while it comes down.

Going up, the retardation is $a_{1}=g(\sin θ+μ\cos θ)$, and the block stops after a distance $d$ with $v_{0}^{2}=2a_{1}d$.

Coming down the same distance $d$, the acceleration is $a_{2}=g(\sin θ-μ\cos θ)$, and $\left (\dfrac{v_{0}}{2}\right )^{2}=2a_{2}d$.

Dividing the two relations:

$\dfrac{a_{1}}{a_{2}}=4\Rightarrow \sin θ+μ\cos θ=4\sin θ-4μ\cos θ\Rightarrow 5μ\cos θ=3\sin θ$

$μ=\dfrac{3}{5}\tan 30^{\circ }=\dfrac{3}{5\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\approx 0.3464$

With $μ=\dfrac{I}{1000}$, $I\approx 346.4$, whose nearest integer is 346.

Hence, the answer is 346.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
When an object is kept at a distance of 30 cm from a concave mirror, the image is formed at a
distance of 10 cm from the mirror. If the object is moved with a speed of 9 cms$^{–1}$, the speed
(in cms$^{–1})$ with which image moves at that instant is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$V_{I} =$ Velocity of image with respect to mirror

$V_{0} =$ Velocity of object with respect to mirror

$|\vec{V_{I}}|=|-\frac{v^{2}}{u^{2}}\vec{V_{0}}|$

$=|-\frac{10\times 10}{30\times 30}\times 9|$

$=1$ cm/s
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot
